- Attachments: prod-issue-capture.xlsx (customer traces), draft playbook (implementation-playbook-v1.pdf).

Action requested: can we run a focused office-hours session that covers:
  1) Where batch size (requests per second vs effective token batching) matters for Redwood runtimes

Proposed slot: Thu 7/22 14:00 PT (30–45m). I dropped the draft playbook and the trace spreadsheet in the thread. If you have a ~10m demo recording we can share, that'd be great to include in the follow-up.

Thanks — will loop in Tae from NRF once we confirm.

Thanks for the invite — the time works for our infra folks. Quick notes from our side after the initial run:

- Batch sizing: our engineers are seeing better throughput when we send larger groups, but latency tails spike for short user flows. We need a recommended policy for mixing synchronous low-latency calls with large async batches.
- KV cache: we realized the team set the TTL too low and was effectively flushing cold cache between bursts. We also have questions about cache placement — in-process vs remote KV for our Kubernetes setup.
- One ask: can you point to a short recording that shows the cache TTL issue? That would help our infra lead (Maya) understand the symptomatic behavior.

We uploaded a side-by-side trace to the folder you mentioned (prod traces were anonymized). Happy to join the office hours and can invite Maya if OK.

Regards,

Hi Tae — great context, thanks.

A few direct answers up front: 
- Mixed workloads: recommend two logical request paths: (A) low-latency fast-path (pin to small batch windows, lower max tokens, local KV where possible) and (B) throughput path (larger batching, async workers, allow slightly higher p50/p90). We'll share the config snippet and a sample autoscaler policy.
- KV TTL & placement: TTL between 30–120s is usually a good starting point for bursty traffic; if your bursts are >5m, consider a remote LRU cache or longer TTL. I'll attach the sample snippet to the playbook.

Attached: prod-issue-capture.xlsx (annotated), and a trimmed 7m clip that demonstrates the cache TTL churn (2027-07-22-quick-win-demo.mp4). Recording of today's office hours (link below) includes Connor's demo — timestamp ~00:06:40 shows the cache churn behavior.

Next steps:
- I can run a 30m deep-dive next Tue (7/27) with Maya + infra (we have a slot at 11:00 PT).
- We'll push a short revision to implementation-playbook-v1.pdf with the three fixes and the rollback matrix.
- HubSpot ticket created: HB-98214 (will log the action items).

On Fri I'll send a one-page summary for NRF execs that frames the cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended near-term changes.

Best,
Sergio
